subject: Routing shim policy, exception ladder, and customer comms
messages:
From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@acme-ops.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME Procurement <procurement@acme-ops.com>
Date: Sat, 27 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Planned model change: clarification on impact and timeline

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the heads up about the upcoming model variant changes in March. We run a fairly latency-sensitive pipeline and a small subset of our requests depend on token-level alignment with the current model. Can you confirm: (1) whether there will be API surface changes we need to code against, (2) whether you support a routing-shim option so our traffic continues hitting the same model family for 30 days, and (3) what the escalation ladder looks like if we detect quality regressions?

We'd like to avoid a forced migration during our month-end processing window (first week of April). Happy to jump on a quick call.

Thanks,
Olivia
Senior ML Engineer
Acme Ops

--
Attachment: acme-migration-timeline.pdf (pdf, 120KB)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@acme-ops.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 27 Feb 2027 12:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Planned model change: clarification on impact and timeline

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear asks. Quick answers up front: (1) No API contract changes are planned for the March variant swap (same REST endpoints/params). (2) We can offer a routing shim (policy-level pin) for 30 days as a limited exception — this requires a short engineering config and a product-approved exception. (3) Escalation ladder: Redwood on-call -> Engineering triage -> Product/CS sync -> Priority rollback window (48h) for verified regressions.

I am looping in product (Marissa) and runtime (Vivek) to: (a) confirm the compatibility checklist we need from Acme, (b) estimate effort to configure a routing shim for your tenant, and (c) propose a customer comms timeline that avoids your month-end. Attached a draft checklist and a proposed shim config for internal review.

Proposed next steps for this thread:
- Olivia: share a short prompt/workload sample and 3 representative requests (privacy-safe) so we can run a quick QA pass.
- Acme procurement: confirm whether you'd like the shim as a paid add-on or covered under current support agreement.
- Marissa/Vivek/Laura: can you confirm feasibility and lead times?

Rishi
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: compatibility-bridge-checklist.xlsx, proposed-routing-shim-config.yml

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@acme-ops.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Mar 2027 10:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Planned model change: confirmation on routing shim feasibility

On Mon, Mar 1, 2027 at 10:18 AM Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com> wrote:
> I am looping in product (Marissa) and runtime (Vivek) to: (a) confirm the compatibility checklist we need from Acme, (b) estimate effort to configure a routing shim for your tenant, and (c) propose a customer comms timeline that avoids your month-end.

Hi all,

Short summary from runtime: the routing shim is technically straightforward — we stand up a per-tenant route that pins to the current model binary and a fallback to the new variant after X days. Estimated work: 1 engineer day to create the policy + 0.5 day ops for testing and rollout. Constraints: (a) shims increase unit cost slightly due to reduced pooling efficiency, (b) we need an explicit exception ticket approved by product/legal for service-level variance, and (c) we should limit shims to 30 days to avoid model drift divergence.

I'll add a simple config template to the ticket (see attached). For QA, we need three representative prompt/response pairs and a perf histogram for the last 7 days. Once we have that, runtime can do a canary run in the staging cluster within 24 hours.

-Vivek
VP, Runtime Engineering

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@acme-ops.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2027 08:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Planned model change: comms plan and exception approval flow

Thanks — a few product notes:
- We'll treat this as a scoped "compatibility exception" rather than a policy change. That means: document the exception in our internal exceptions log, notify CSM and account exec, and require a post-shim quality report from the customer at day 15 and day 30.
- Legal will need to sign off on the service-level variance language; Laura, can you draft the short amendment? We should avoid changing pricing in the amendment; instead list the shim as a temporary configuration add-on and bill under existing committed capacity unless procurement requests otherwise.
- Communications: propose we (a) send a short comms window plan to Acme by EOD Tuesday (their time), (b) do a 30-minute tech sync Wednesday to collect sample prompts, and (c) schedule the shim deployment for next Friday to finish before Acme's month-end window.

Marissa
Head of Product
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@acme-ops.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2027 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Planned model change: comms plan and exception approval flow

Hi team—

I drafted a brief amendment and exception statement that covers (1) the 30-day routing shim, (2) rollback window and verification requirements, and (3) cost disclosure for reduced pooling efficiency. Sending the draft to Acme (cc'ed) and procurement now. Olivia — if procurement prefers a PO amendment, let us know. Otherwise we'll proceed with the short amendment and schedule the tech sync for Wednesday 11:00 AM PT.

Laura Bennett
Head of Legal Operations
Redwood Inference

--
